name: Modbus Client → Send
description: This action queues a custom Modbus frame for transmission and optionally handles the outcome.

config_entries.label: Address
config_entries.description: The device address the frame is sent to. Accepts `0`-`255`; the valid Modbus device range is `1`-`247`, and `0` is broadcast (never answered unless one of the broadcast options below is set; see [Behavior](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client/#behavior)).

config_entries.label: Modbus ID
config_entries.description: The Modbus hub to send on. Automatically assigned when a single hub is configured.

config_entries.label: Pdu
config_entries.description: The PDU to send: function code followed by data. The device address and CRC are added automatically - do **not** include them. Maximum 253 bytes (the Modbus PDU limit): an empty or over-long YAML list fails config validation. As a lambda it must return a `modbus::helpers::PduBuffer` (a fixed-capacity stack vector, not `std::vector`): `return {0x03, 0x00, 0x10, 0x00, 0x01};` works, and so does directly returning the result of a `modbus::helpers::create_*_pdu()` builder - see [Building PDUs with Helpers](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client/#building-pdus-with-helpers). Unlike the YAML list, a lambda result isn't length-checked: one over 253 bytes is silently truncated to the limit rather than rejected. An empty lambda result (or a builder that fails - see below) also produces an empty PDU; the hub refuses to send it, and `on_not_sent` fires.

config_entries.label: Allow Broadcast Read
config_entries.description: Let a read be sent to address `0` and wait for its reply, for a device that answers the broadcast address - see [Broadcast](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client/#behavior) under Behavior. Applies to the function codes whose reply carries data (the reads, including `0x17`): a literal `pdu` with any other code is rejected at config time, and a lambda-built one is sent without it. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Continuous
config_entries.description: Poll continuously instead of sending once - see [Continuous polling](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client/#continuous-polling). Cannot be used with known write function codes. They are rejected at config time when the PDU is a literal list, or sent non-continuously at run time with a warning when it comes from a lambda; every other code - read, custom, vendor-specific, or unknown - is allowed to poll continuously. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Expect Broadcast Write Response
config_entries.description: Wait for the reply to a write sent to address `0` instead of treating it as fire-and-forget - see [Broadcast](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client/#behavior) under Behavior. Applies to the function codes whose reply carries no data (the plain writes and custom codes): a literal `pdu` with any other code is rejected at config time, and a lambda-built one is sent without it. Defaults to `false`.
